While our confidence intervals capture a substantial range of likely outcomes, specific high-impact events or unforeseen developments could certainly push the actual results outside these stated boundaries. For instance, an unexpectedly significant positive development, such as a major technological breakthrough, a sudden resolution of a significant geopolitical conflict, or an unforeseen economic stimulus package, could lead to an outcome substantially higher than our upper bounds. Conversely, a severe negative shock like a sudden financial crisis, an escalation of a major geopolitical conflict, a widespread natural disaster, or a completely unexpected adverse policy change could drive the outcome significantly lower than our stated lower bounds. These types of "black swan" events, by their very nature, are difficult to predict and incorporate into standard probabilistic models, representing the most significant risks to the validity of any forecast.
